name: VelozaPay — Crypto Payments for WooCommerce
author: VelozaPay

sections.description:
VelozaPay lets your WooCommerce store accept cryptocurrency payments, with the money going straight to a wallet you own. There is no sign-up, no KYC, and no chargebacks.

It works like any other WooCommerce payment method. When a customer chooses crypto at checkout, VelozaPay shows them a clean payment page on your own store — they pick a coin, scan the QR code, and pay. The order is marked paid automatically once the payment is confirmed on the blockchain, and the customer never has to leave your site.

To get started, install the plugin and add the wallet addresses where you would like to be paid. That is all there is to it.

What you get

  • Accept Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT, USDC, Solana, Litecoin, Dogecoin, Bitcoin Cash and POL (Polygon)
  • The payment page runs on your own store — customers never leave your domain
  • Payments settle on-chain straight to your wallet; VelozaPay never holds your money
  • No KYC, no monthly fees, no chargebacks
  • Instant approval — no application or merchant review
  • Instant access — accept payments the same day you install
  • A QR-code payment page with a live status the customer can follow
  • Works with both the classic checkout and the WooCommerce Blocks checkout
  • Translation-ready

Every cryptocurrency has a small minimum payment amount, since very tiny on-chain payments are not practical. You can see the current minimum for each coin in the minimum order amounts guide.

External services

VelozaPay processes crypto payments through the VelozaPay payment service at api.velozapay.com. When an order is paid, the plugin sends only the order amount, currency and your payout wallet address so the payment can be created — no customer personal data is shared. By using the plugin you agree to the VelozaPay Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the velozapay folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Payments and enable VelozaPay Crypto.
  4. Open the gateway settings and enter at least one crypto payout wallet address.
  5. Save. Your store can now accept crypto payments.
sections.faq:
Does VelozaPay hold my money?

No. VelozaPay is fully non-custodial. Every payment settles on-chain directly to the wallet address you configure. The plugin only ever stores public wallet addresses — never private keys.

Do I need to pass KYC?

No KYC is required to receive cryptocurrency payments. Install the plugin, add a wallet address, and you can start accepting payments the same day.

Which cryptocurrencies are supported?

Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), USDT, USDC, Litecoin (LTC), Dogecoin (DOGE), Bitcoin Cash (BCH), Solana (SOL) and POL (Polygon). USDT can be paid on the Tron, Ethereum, BNB Chain, Polygon and Solana networks; USDC on the Ethereum, BNB Chain, Polygon, Base and Solana networks.

Is there a minimum payment amount?

Yes. Each cryptocurrency has a small minimum, because very tiny payments are not practical to send on-chain. You can check the current minimum for every coin in the minimum order amounts guide.

Are there monthly fees?

No. The plugin is free and there are no monthly or setup fees. A small flat percentage applies per transaction only when you receive a payment.

Does it work with the WooCommerce Blocks checkout?

Yes. VelozaPay works with both the classic shortcode checkout and the modern WooCommerce Blocks checkout.
sections.changelog:
1.0.1

  • Fixed: the minimum-amount check could be skipped if the network lookup failed, allowing an order below the network minimum to be paid. Such payments are never forwarded and cannot be recovered, so the check now fails closed.
  • Fixed: the minimum shown and enforced is now the one that applies to this plugin’s payment route, which is higher than the base network minimum.
  • Added: below-minimum errors now name the exact minimum and coin instead of a generic message.
  • Added: unconfirmed (pending) payment notifications are acknowledged but never mark an order paid.
  • Changed: payment notifications are acknowledged in the plain-text format the payment network expects, preventing repeated callbacks.

1.0.0

  • First public release of VelozaPay.
